          Tottenham vs Arsenal Prediction: WSL North London Derby Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to the first WSL north London derby of the 2026-27 season with our Tottenham vs Arsenal prediction and preview.

The season could hardly be going worse for Renée Slegers and her Arsenal side as they travel to Tottenham with their hopes of salvaging a disastrous start to the Women's Super League campaign hanging in the balance.
For the first time in league history, Spurs will begin a north London derby above Arsenal in the league table, though both sides will both be looking to arrest their recent form.

Arsenal are on the brink of making more unwanted history, without a win in five WSL matches for the first time (D3 L2) and have drawn more English top-flight games than any other side since the start of last season (9).
They have also never failed to win at least two of their opening seven matches of a WSL campaign, a record now under serious threat.

Having started the campaign so promisingly, unbeaten in their first four matches (W3 D1), Martin Ho will also be desperate for a response from his side after two bruising league outings at London City and Chelsea. In doing so, Spurs became just the second team in WSL history to concede six or more goals in consecutive matches, following Doncaster Rovers Belles in 2013.

While those recent results have exposed some worrying defensive vulnerabilities, scoring goals has certainly not been Tottenham's problem. Only Manchester City (19) have scored more WSL goals than Spurs (18) this season, but only Charlton (18) have conceded more than their 14.
It is an extraordinary contrast. Before this season, no team in WSL history had scored at least 15 goals while conceding 10 or more in their opening six matches.
At the heart of Spurs attacking masterclasses has been captain Drew Spence (215 currently), who could equal Millie Bright (216) for the most appearances made in WSL history.
The contrast with Arsenal could hardly be greater.

While Tottenham have been scoring freely despite their defensive struggles, the Gunners have been remarkably toothless in front of goal, with their inability to turn chances into goals becoming one of the defining problems of their season.

Despite attempting the third-most shots in the WSL this season (121), Arsenal have the worst shot conversion rate in the competition (4.1%), alongside the third-worst shooting accuracy (30.6%) and third-lowest average expected goals (xG) per shot (0.09).
It represents a dramatic decline for a side that ranked among the top two in the WSL for shot conversion in each of the previous two campaigns.
Perhaps nowhere is that struggle more evident than with Alessia Russo.

Last season's golden boot runner-up has found goals hard to come by with just one to her name across six matchdays, and her frustrating afternoon against Birmingham City summed up Arsenal's attacking difficulties. Russo managed just two attempts, neither of which tested the goalkeeper. Remarkably, she has already gone three WSL matches without registering a shot on target this season, having done so only four times across the whole of 2025-26.

Nonetheless, her record against their rivals offers promise; she has scored more league goals against Tottenham (eight) than any other side, and never has she failed to score at least two goals across her first seven top-flight outings of a campaign.
Furthemore, Slegers is unbeaten in all 17 of her WSL games against English managers(W11 D6), with only Sonia Bompastor (18) facing English coaches moreoften without losing in the competition.
Saturday could also bring an unwanted milestone, with the Dutchwoman at risk of going five matches without a win as Arsenal manager in all competitions for the first time.

Their inability to find a breakthrough is reflected in how their matches have unfolded; the Gunners have spent 61% of their playing time with the scores level, more than any other WSL side this season.
Even more remarkably, when matches are tied, Arsenal boast the best shot difference per 90 minutes in the competition (+15), yet still have a negative goal difference per 90 (-0.25).
